title: Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement: Service Level and Implementation Commitments
content:
Paystride commits, under the Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement, to a monthly platform availability and to a go-live target, with credits where a commitment is missed.

| | Starter | Growth | Professional | Enterprise | Enterprise Plus | Strategic |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly platform availability commitment (percent) | 99.5 | 99.5 | 99.7 | 99.9 | 99.9 | 99.95 |
| Calendar days after the end of the affected month within which the employer must claim an SLA credit | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Business days after contract within which Paystride commits to go live, if the employer delivers its payroll file on time | 10 | 15 | 30 | 45 | 60 | 90 |
| Credit, as percent of the implementation fee, when go-live misses the target for reasons on Paystride's side | 0 | 0 | 10 | 10 | 15 | 20 |

## Service level credit ladder

The same ladder applies on every tier. It maps the measured monthly availability band to a credit expressed as a percent of that month's platform fee after discounts; the lowest band reached applies.

| Measured monthly availability | Credit (percent of the month's platform fee after discounts) |
|---|---|
| below the tier's commitment | 10 |
| below 99.0 | 25 |
| below 95.0 | 50 |

## Reading the ladder

Because the lowest band reached applies, a month measured at 98.4 percent availability on a hypothetical Professional-tier program is below the commitment of 99.7 and below 99.0 but not below 95.0, so the ladder gives 25 percent. A month at 99.6 percent is below the Enterprise commitment of 99.9 and gives 10 percent there, while on a Growth-tier program, whose commitment is 99.5, it is not below the commitment.
